reviews.title: UPDATE MAC APP from 1950’s version
reviews.text: Five stars on iOS, where Endel is genuinely part of how I work, but the Mac app is letting the side down. On iPhone I can drop a soundscape straight into a Shortcut and trigger Focus or Relax from an automation, which is exactly what you want from a focus tool. On Mac there is no equivalent. The app exposes nothing to the macOS Shortcuts app, so there is no way to start a mode, switch between modes, or wire Endel into a work and break routine without clicking the window by hand. There is no URL scheme for mode selection either, so even a scripted workaround is off the table. The fix is the App Intents you already ship on iOS, just added to the Mac target so Focus, Relax, Study and the rest show up as Shortcuts actions on the desktop. App Intents is cross platform, so for a team that already has the iOS side working this is small. I am a lifetime supporter and I will happily keep singing about Endel, but please close the gap on Mac. It is the one thing stopping it being seamless.

I have paid for Endel premium for the past couple of years, but I’m getting frustrated with the direction they seem to be taking.

I don't care about merchandise, and if I want to upgrade to lifetime or invite friends, I'll go and find the option in the settings. None of that should be forced upon me on load, nor exist on my home screen. If you insist on doing so, at least give paying customers the option to opt out and turn it off.

On top of that, the MacOS app has been "updated" but as far as I can tell as a user, it seems to be a downgrade, and is simply a mirror of the web app. It might well be more efficient, and use less CPU power, but personally I never noticed an issue with performance that I felt needed fixing anyway. Instead most of the features that made it worth having a native app have been removed. What benefit does the app now bring over loading the browser version?

Apparently these features are going to be brought back in a future update, but why not wait until these features are ready in the rebuilt and updated version before you release the “upgraded” app? I don't deny that a rewrite and performance improvements are a great thing, but at least ensure you carry the existing features over to the new version.

reviews.title: At least one trial session should be included…
reviews.text: Trial available only for yearly subscriptions. Of the product is that good as claimed, surely no need to be that pushy. Too much gimmicky gamification for the type of app (shake the tree to see our offers). It seems it might have value, but I’ll never know…

reviews.title: Spamming deals after I purchased a subscription already
reviews.text: The app keeps spamming deals for lifetime subscription after I purchased a yearly subscription already. And there is no way to turn it off. Why am I paying if I’m getting an add every five seconds! I’m quitting this app as soon as I find a suitable alternative.
